key_insight: A new CALPHAD-based Γ ductility metric better correlates with tensile ductility in refractory compositionally complex alloys than the DFT-based D-parameter, while performing equally well in compression.
engineering_relevance: The metric could guide selection of refractory alloys that combine high-temperature performance with room-temperature tensile ductility.
method: Combine the BCC–HCP free-energy difference, (110) BCC surface interfacial free energy, and electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion.
Compare Γ with established ductility metrics for tensile and compressive plasticity.
Propose combining Γ with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility to capture intrinsic and extrinsic ductility contributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a modest improvement in tensile-ductility correlation over the D-parameter and comparable compression performance, without numerical evaluation details.
watch_item: The proposed oxygen-solubility extension is a first-order approach, not an established predictor of oxygen-induced embrittlement.
paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
